p030-032b.name: Part 1's intro line with the Red Line's first paragraph, try 2: the two pronouns named
p030-032b.text:
To see what each tool does, let's look first at what goes wrong in the brain under trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress, since those "Hardware Failures" are what this protocol is built to fix.

If you've tried to talk yourself out of a trigger and couldn't, it's because blood flow in your brain shifts away from the Cortex, which handles logic and reasoning, toward the Brainstem, the part that keeps you alive. That happens once your heart rate climbs above its usual resting rate, or its variability drops (a smartwatch shows both), and the shift lasts until you calm down. Perry describes the point where that happens as a "Metabolic Red Line" for the traumatized brain, and calls the state past it "Fear".
p030-032b.diagnosis: try 1 (#333, https://www.pangram.com/history/31cf2d57-7b85-46e3-951b-613e14624ca3) read Low over the intro line, where "since those Hardware Failures are what it's built to fix" lets "it" be the brain, and Medium over "That happens once ...", where "and it lasts" can be the heart rate or the shift: each named ("this protocol", "the shift")
p030-032b.decides: whether naming the two things a reader could take two ways takes the pair to High in every window
p030-032b.tells: a list of three in the intro (trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress: the protocol's scope); a long condition before the point in the second sentence of the paragraph
p030-032b.human_tells: none to name: the words are mine and the post's
p030-032b.first_fix: payoff: the intro opens on what the reader gets (what each tool does), the paragraph on the reader's own failure and what happens while triggered; join: the label tied into the intro's sentence ("since those Hardware Failures are what it's built to fix"); plain: "the part of your brain that reasons goes offline" for "anatomy overrides intellect", "above its usual resting rate" for "your resting heart rate goes up"
p030-032b.humanized: the intro opens on what the reader gets ("To see what each tool in this protocol does"), the reader inside it ("let's look first"), its label tied in as what the protocol fixes; and the paragraph after it: the reason the reader asks for comes straight after their own failure, in the same sentence ("it's because blood flow in your brain shifts"); when it happens and that it passes, tied on with "That happens"; the Cortex and the Brainstem each explained where first used, the two glosses built differently; Perry's names last, once the reader has the thing they name; plain words for the abstract ones ("the part that keeps you alive" for "runs survival")

p033b.name: The Red Line's second paragraph by itself, try 2: the doubt said once
p033b.text: So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off. Above the line your functional IQ drops a lot, and stress chemicals called catecholamines flood the Nucleus Accumbens, a reward center deep in the brain. There they set off the making of DeltaFosB, the protein researchers suspect holds the armor in place. Only work on your trauma while you're under that line, which trauma therapists call staying in your "window of tolerance".
p033b.diagnosis: try 1 (#335, https://www.pangram.com/history/58a89835-e138-4a23-b512-6369e1c9eda9) read AI Low over the DeltaFosB sentence, which said the doubt twice ("may be what holds ..., though the research on that isn't settled"), as the read against his fixes had marked (way 9, 16); said once, in "suspect"
p033b.decides: whether the doubt said once takes the AI window to Human; the Low windows on either side are the next tries
p033b.tells: "instead of taking it off" (a contrast, though it answers what the reader expects processing to do); a long second sentence
p033b.human_tells: none to name: the words are mine and the post's
p033b.first_fix: payoff: the claim, then why (above the line), then what to do; join: the caveat into the clause it qualifies ("though the research on that isn't settled"); plain: "set off the making of DeltaFosB" for "transcribe new DeltaFosB proteins", "stress chemicals called catecholamines", "only work on your trauma while you're under that line" for "staying within a manageable window of tolerance rather than overwhelming activation"
